issues_detected.description: No dataset-level persistent identifier (DOI/RRID). Findability relies on the project landing page (https://chorus4ai.org/) rather than a registered dataset DOI. The only DOI present (10.1007/s12028-024-02007) is a Springer publication DOI, not a dataset DOI.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a dataset-level DOI (e.g., via DataCite/PhysioNet) so the dataset itself is citable and resolvable independent of the project site.

issues_detected.description: Version tracking lacks an explicit version identifier. version_access and updates describe controlled, evolving releases (45K to target 100K+ admissions) but no version number, errata, or release notes are provided.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add explicit version identifiers with dated release notes and errata for each enclave release to strengthen provenance.

issues_detected.description: Human-subject representation gives instance counts and subgroup structure (by hospital, by ICU/PICU/NICU) but no quantified demographics (age/sex/race distributions) or explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add demographic distributions and formal inclusion/exclusion criteria to fully characterize the cohort.

semantic_insights: Description is highly specific: 20 academic centers (14 data acquisition centers), 100,000+ patient target, 45,000 unique admissions and 50,000 released admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 23 TB waveform data, 7,642 radiology admissions (as of August 2025).
NIH grant OT2OD032701 (project 1OT2OD032701-01) follows the NIH Other Transaction (OT2) award format correctly and is consistent across funders, license, ip_restrictions, and retention_limit.
Publication DOI prefix 10.1007 correctly corresponds to Springer (Neurocritical Care journal); format is valid.
Controlled-access model (institutional-email registration + signed DUA + secure Azure enclave) is consistent with the clinical PHI sensitivity, HIPAA, and 45 CFR 46 obligations declared.

Deidentification methods are appropriate and modality-specific: OMOP CDM transformation + privacy_scan_tool for EHR, OHNLP tokenization for notes, DICOM header de-id for imaging, WFDB/EDF+ controlled access for signals.

involves_human_subjects=true is corroborated by ethical_reviews (IRB at 14 sites), informed_consent (waiver-of-consent framework), and at_risk_populations (pediatric/neonatal) — cross-field human-subjects logic is satisfied.
Multi-modal standard formats (OMOP CDM, WFDB, DICOM, OHNLP, EDF+/Persyst) each cite a published or open-source schema, giving strong interoperability evidence.
